correctness.rationale: DLMF 19.12.2 gives the exact endpoint expansion with complementary modulus \(k'=|\gamma|\), yielding the stated derivatives. Strict negativity of \(\epsilon''\) on a punctured neighborhood makes \(a=\epsilon'(\gamma)\) invertible. The exact support identities \(b=\epsilon-\gamma a\), \(g'=-\gamma\), and \(g''=-1/\epsilon''\) give \(g''(a)\sim4\pi/\log(1/|a|)\). The limit \(\gamma/a\to0\) supplies \(g''(0)=0\), while \(g'''=\epsilon'''/(\epsilon'')^3\) diverges. The semialgebraicity contradiction uses the source's own reduction plus Newton--Puiseux.
